sentences.text:
----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Mahendra Shandilya through V.C.
 Mr. Himanshu Ranjan Singh Bhati

For Respondent(s) : Mr. Lalit Kishore Sen, Public  Prosecutor  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE CHANDRA PRAKASH SHRIMALI Order 09/05/2025 This application for anticipatory bail under Section 482 of the BNSS (old Section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the petitioner apprehending his arrest in connection with F.I.R.
No.61/2024, registered at Police Station Gachhipura, District - Nagaur for the offences under Sections 420, 409 & 120B of the IPC.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that as per the case of the prosecution, the allegations against the present petitioner Bajrang Singh are that he had created his own app by the name 'TMC'
on the Play Store, a company which was not officially registered.
On the said app new IDs were created for all customers on this app.
The accused-petitioner Bajrang Singh [2025:RJ-JD:22586] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-4492/2025] received the maximum amount of investment for the said 'TMT' and 'TMC' companies in cash.
The allegation against the accused petitioner is that he along with other co-accused persons has cheated the hard earned money of the complainant and other persons which was about 39 lacs.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the accused-petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The whole story of the prosecution is false and concocted.
He never run any business by the name and style of aforesaid companies.

Therefore, he prayed that the anticipatory bail application filed on behalf of the petitioner may be allowed and he may be released on bail.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor vehemently opposed the bail application and submitted that accused has committed a serious crime committing fraud with the complainant and other persons by cheating their hard earned money.

Therefore, he prayed that looking to the gravity of the offence,
benefit of bail may not be extended to the petitioner.
benefit of anticipatory bail may not be extended to him.
From perusal of the material available on record, this Court finds that petitioner Bajrang Singh created his own app by the name 'TMC' company which was not officially registered.
He used to conduct Zoom meetings from Jaipur.

During the investigation, it was prima facie found from the bank statement of the account of complainant Parmeshwar that a total amount of Rs.1,41,131/- was deposited in the account of Arvind Singh, the brother of the accused-petitioner Bajrang Singh.
The business of both 'TMT' and [2025:RJ-JD:22586] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-4492/2025] 'TMC' companies were solely managed by the accused-petitioner Bajrang Singh.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the accused-petitioner at this stage.
The anticipatory bail application is, therefore, rejected.
(CHANDRA PRAKASH SHRIMALI),J 167-Ramesh Goyal, P.S.
